message.content:
Yes—Atlanta residents can file a noise‑complaint with the city’s authorities.  
Here’s how you can do it:

| Step | What to do | Where / How |
|------|------------|-------------|
| **1** | **Check the city’s noise ordinance** | The City of Atlanta’s Noise Enforcement page lists the permitted hours, decibel limits, and the types of violations that can be reported. <https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/police/noise-enforcement> |
| **2** | **File an online complaint** | Use the “Noise Complaint” form on the Atlanta Police Department’s website. <https://www.atlantaga.gov/department/Police> (look for “Noise Enforcement” or “Complaint Form”). |
| **3** | **Call the non‑emergency line** | 404‑656‑4000 – this line connects you to the Atlanta Police Department’s Noise Enforcement Unit. |
| **4** | **Visit City Hall (optional)** | If you prefer in‑person, you can go to the City Hall at 1000 Peachtree Street NE, Atlanta, GA 30308, and speak with the Police Department or Code Enforcement staff. |
| **5** | **Follow up** | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy if you need to check the status or provide additional information. |

### Quick Tips

* **Time matters:** Most noise complaints are taken seriously during nighttime hours (typically 10 p.m.–6 a.m.) and on weekends.  
* **Decibel limits:** The city’s ordinance sets specific decibel thresholds for residential and commercial areas.  
* **Documentation:** If possible, note the time, location, and nature of the noise (e.g., construction, loud music, barking dogs). This helps officers assess the situation quickly.

If you’re unsure whether your situation qualifies as a violation, you can call the non‑emergency line first; the dispatcher will advise whether a formal complaint is warranted.
